# Tasks: issue-398-ci-review-use-antigravity-as-independent

Scope: tasks 1-8 are this implementation. Tasks 9-11 are OWNER steps that need a
variable change this proposal does not authorize, so they are not part of this
implementation. Tasks 12-14 are activation and are DEFERRED: they start only
after Agy review capacity is restored (limits are currently exhausted) and the
owner records a separate activation decision. Order: hardening, shadow, isolated
fixture, preview pilot, owner decision.

Owner-only tasks (marked OWNER) change permissions, installations, variables,
required checks or rulesets. Each needs its own explicit owner authorization and
is never done by the implementer. Code tasks need independent review before
merge. No task weakens a review gate or substitutes a bot review for a required
human approval. Nothing here approves, re-reviews or merges
mctlhq/mctl-gitops#3023.

## Tests

All local tests use synthetic API responses in `.github/tests/test_review_gate_controller.py` / `test_agy_formal_reviews.py`, run by `workflow-tests.yml`. Live items are only in the deferred tasks 12-13; T1-T18 are synthetic and are part of this implementation.

- [ ] T1. Trusted unedited Claude PASS on the live head goes to `pass_check`, with no dispatch.
- [ ] T2. Claude `CHANGES_REQUESTED` (P1/P2) plus a qualifying Agy PASS gives `fail_check` (blocking precedence).
- [ ] T3. Claude `NO_VERDICT_TRANSIENT` (both tokens exhausted) plus a qualifying formal exact-head/digest Agy PASS gives `pass_check` via reuse. Without one, it gives a single `dispatch` pinned to the head.
- [ ] T4. Claude caller without `Classify outcome:` steps and a green run gives `NO_VERDICT_OTHER`, reason `caller pinned before outcome classifier`, no dispatch (reproduces mctlhq/mctl-gitops#3023).
- [ ] T5. Agy outcomes P1/P2, no verdict, malformed or truncated output, stale head or base, unavailable runner, auth failure or unreadable API give no approval and a failed or pending check. The terminal guard prevents re-dispatch until head or digest moves or `force_rerun`.
- [ ] T6. `is_trusted_reusable_ref` with a SHA not on main, and with a compare error, returns untrusted. Mutation: remove the predicate and confirm T6 turns red, then restore.
- [ ] T7. Informational Agy comment, a check from another integration, a carried mark, a forged `agy-formal:` marker in an edited review, or a PR-uploaded artifact each give no reuse.
- [ ] T8. Merge-queue dispatch with `check_name=independent-review`: carry from a trusted Claude PASS when parents are `[base, head]` and the file and blob sets match. Any mismatch runs a fresh review, and a carried mark is never re-carried.
- [ ] T9. Shadow side effects: with missing baseline the controller evaluates, writes only `independent-review-shadow` with the `baseline missing` text, and dispatches nothing. In the PR-head, merge-queue, missing-baseline and error paths the publisher writes only `independent-review-shadow` and makes no `POST .../reviews` and no dismissal call (asserted on the recorded API calls and by a static test).
- [ ] T10. Enforce with missing baseline or an unbound `independent-review` raises `Unknown`, with no writes.
- [ ] T11. Metrics: `queue_wait_seconds` and `time_to_valid_verdict_seconds` computed from fixture timestamps; `fallback_rate` unchanged.
- [ ] T12. Duplicate ticks, replayed dispatch events and concurrent Claude and Agy results produce one effective check per (repo, PR, head, mode, digest). A head push cancels unstarted superseded runs and never marks the old head successful.
- [ ] T13. A PR authored by the reviewer App identity gives `fail_check` (no self-approval).
- [ ] T14. Privileged jobs: assert by static workflow test that no job holding `AGY_REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` checks out PR refs or runs on `pull_request`, and that the model job has no App token.
- [ ] T15. Mutation tests: disable blocking precedence, the head binding in reuse, the transient-only dispatch allowlist, the ancestry check, the policy boundary check, the gate-completion recheck and the shadow early return, one at a time. Confirm the corresponding tests fail, then restore and confirm green.
- [ ] T16. Policy boundary: a reviewer SHA that is on main but older than the boundary, an unset boundary, and a boundary compare error each return untrusted; the run is not counted and does not trigger the fallback.
- [ ] T17. A blocking `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review that appears while a PASS is being published: the publisher dismisses its own approval (enforce), the check is not completed as successful, and in shadow no review is posted at all.
- [ ] T18. Head or digest movement (or base movement under strict-base policy), or a changed check owner, between verdict and gate completion gives no success write; without strict-base policy a base-only move still completes the check for the live head and digest; a stale or replayed event, dispatch or run attempt is ignored; a failed or partial read gives `UNKNOWN`.

## Rollback

- Code (tasks 2-6a): revert in reverse order: first the 8b and 6b boundary PRs (if merged), then the 2-6a `.github` PR. The previous controller behaviour is fail-closed, and consumers pinned to the reverted SHA keep working because it stays on main history.
- Caller bumps (7-8): revert the pin in the consumer repo. This only loses the classifier, which means no fallback, not wrong approvals.
- Shadow (9-10): set `AGY_REVIEW_GATE_ENABLED` to anything other than `true` (kill switch; scheduled runs become `skipped`). Remove the repo from `AGY_REVIEW_GATE_REPOS`. `independent-review-shadow` is not required, so leftover checks are harmless.
- Enforce pilot (deferred tasks 12-13, when activated): switch the repo back to `:shadow`, then the owner removes only the added `independent-review` context from the ruleset. `agy-formal-review` and all other checks, the review count, stale dismissal and the merge queue are never touched by rollback. If the App is compromised, revoke the `AGY_REVIEW_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` or uninstall the App per the plan's rollback section. Never mark a check green manually or post a substitute approval to unblock a PR. Re-run a real review instead.
